title: [AMD] fix: use the hardware fp8 e4m3 convert on gfx950
body:
## Motivation


`pack_fp8` is the fp8 quantization step in the DSv4, DSv3.2-indexer, MiniMax and Kimi-K3 kernels. On ROCm it is a hand-written bit twiddle, and it converts part of its input range wrong.

The overflow check is `exp8 >= kMaxExp`, and that is off by one. `exp8 == kMaxExp` is not overflow, it is the top exponent of the format, and e4m3 holds plenty of values there. So on gfx950 everything from 256 to 448 gets written out as 448. At the bottom of that range, that is 75% too big. Rounding is biased upward as well: ties go away from zero instead of to even, and one bf16 input in sixteen lands exactly on a tie.

body:
# [AMD] Accept row-strided views in RMSNorm aiter path

## Motivation

`RMSNorm.forward_aiter` clones any non-contiguous input to contiguous before calling
aiter's `rmsnorm2d_fwd`. But `rmsnorm2d_fwd` is row-wise and only requires the last
dim to be unit-stride; a 2D view with contiguous rows but a strided row pitch — e.g. a
q_lora / kv_a slice split from a packed QKV-a projection — is already valid input. The
clone is a wasted per-layer `contiguous()` copy on the DeepSeek MLA prefill path.

## Modifications

Relax the guard to only clone when the last dim itself is strided (`stride(-1) != 1`)
or the view is higher-rank:

```python
elif not x.is_contiguous() and x.stride(-1) != 1:
    x = x.contiguous()
```

Output is bit-identical for the unit-last-dim case (aiter `rmsnorm2d_fwd` is row-wise
and reads row-strided input correctly).

Remove both staging copies from the modular MoE symmetric reduce-scatter path, building on #46703:

```text
Before: expert output → copy to registered input → ReduceScatter → copy to final output
```

## Summary

The 3D decode path in unified attention splits the softmax across parallel segments to widen a launch grid that would otherwise be only as large as the KV head count. title: dsv4: merge c4 prefill compress+write into a single launch
```
body:
## Summary

Under prefill / `target_verify`, the ratio=4 (indexer) compress path launches
two independent kernels back-to-back:

- `flash_c4_prefill` — compress epilogue (compact output, one row per plan)
- `write_c4_prefill` — ring-buffer staging write

The **decode** path already fuses these inline (`flash_c4_decode`). This PR does
the same for **prefill** by grid-concatenating the two domains into a single
launch: blocks `[0, num_c_blocks)` run the compress epilogue, the trailing
```
